panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Figure 1A is a peripheral blood smear depicting marked lymphocytosis composed of pleomorphic mature-looking lymphoid cells, a characteristic finding in this case of neonatal ALPS. B: Figure 1B displays atypical circulating lymphocytes exhibiting marked nuclear irregularities and multilobated forms, which are morphologic features associated with this ALPS case. C: Figure 1C shows lymphocytes with cytoplasmic projections or pseudopods, another specific atypical morphologic finding in the context of the ALPS presentation.

panels.figure_caption: Peripheral blood smear, wright stain depicts moderate normocytic normochromic anemia with leukocytosis, and marked lymphocytosis composed of pleomorphic mature-looking lymphoid cells (A); many atypical forms showing marked nuclear irregularities with multilobated forms (flower-like cells) (B); and/or cytoplasmic projections/pseudopods (C).
in_text_mentions: (serial CBCs are summarized in Table 1); the white blood cell count (WBC) at birth was 29 × 103/µl, lymphocytes 20.6 × 103/µl, eosinophils 0.6 × 103/µl, hemoglobin (Hb) 12.2 g/dl, and platelets 73 × (103/µl). Peripheral smear (Figure 1) showed moderate normocytic normochromic anemia with leukocytosis, significant eosinophilia, and marked lymphocytosis composed of pleomorphic mature-looking lymphoid cells (Figure 1A), with prominent atypical forms showing cytoplasmic projections/pseudopods (Figure 1B) and/or marked nuclear irregularities with multilobated forms (flower-like cells) (Figure 1C).

To our knowledge, the distinct morphologic features of circulating lymphocytes demonstrated in our patient (Figure 1) have not been described in previous literature in ALPS patients (11). These morphologic findings significantly resolved after initial therapy with sirolimus, in parallel with reduction in DNT percentages by flow cytometry, which indicate that the abnormal DNTs are probably those with the abnormal morphology.
